flashcards.q: How many bytes per parameter does full fine-tuning with Adam need, and what's the 7B/70B memory cost?
flashcards.a: ~16-18 bytes/param (bf16 weight + bf16 grad + fp32 master weight + fp32 momentum + fp32 variance), before activations. 7B ~112-140GB, 70B ~1.1-1.4TB.

flashcards.q: What is the LoRA forward-pass formula and why is B initialized to zero?
flashcards.a: h = Wx + (alpha/r) * B A x. B starts at zero (A is small random) so delta W = 0 at step 0 -- the model is numerically identical to the frozen base at the start of training, which keeps training stable.

flashcards.q: Worked example: LoRA parameter count vs full FT for a 4096x4096 matrix at rank 8.
flashcards.a: Full FT: 4096x4096 = 16.8M params. LoRA r=8: 4096x8 + 8x4096 = 65,536 params -- about a 256x reduction for that matrix.

flashcards.q: What are the three specific tricks QLoRA adds beyond plain LoRA?
flashcards.a: 1) NF4: 4-bit quantization with bins at normal-distribution quantiles (fits pretrained weight stats). 2) Double quantization: quantizes the per-block scaling constants to 8-bit, saving ~0.37 bits/param (~3GB on a 65B model). 3) Paged optimizers: page Adam state to CPU RAM on gradient-checkpointing memory spikes instead of OOMing.

flashcards.q: QLoRA memory: 7B and 70B model sizes, roughly?
flashcards.a: 7B QLoRA ~12GB. 70B QLoRA ~35-48GB -- fits on a single 80GB GPU, versus ~1.1-1.4TB for full FT of the 70B model.

flashcards.q: How does DoRA decompose a weight matrix, and why does it add zero inference latency?
flashcards.a: W = m * (V / ||V||): a learned per-column magnitude m times a unit-norm direction V. LoRA is applied only to the direction; magnitude is learned separately. Because both are linear compositions on the frozen base, DoRA merges into a single weight matrix at inference exactly like plain LoRA -- no extra runtime compute.

flashcards.q: Why does DoRA outperform LoRA at matched rank?
flashcards.a: Full fine-tuning changes a weight's magnitude and direction somewhat independently; a single additive low-rank LoRA update tends to change both together in a way that doesn't match that pattern. DoRA's explicit magnitude/direction split tracks full-FT's update pattern more closely, closing most of the remaining quality gap.

flashcards.q: What is the 2026 practical default LoRA configuration, and when should rank go higher?
flashcards.a: r=16, alpha=16, DoRA enabled, target_modules=all-linear. Raise to r=32-64 for complex multi-turn, code, or math tasks -- 2025 research found intermediate ranks give a better capacity/stability tradeoff than the smaller 8-16 range from the original paper.

flashcards.q: Why does targeting all linear layers (not just attention Q/V) matter more than rank in some cases?
flashcards.a: The original LoRA paper only adapted attention query/value projections. Adapting all linear layers including MLP up/down/gate projections closes more of the gap to full FT, especially on tasks stressing MLP capacity like code and math.

flashcards.q: What is catastrophic forgetting and how does LoRA compare to full FT on it?
flashcards.a: Fine-tuning on a narrow distribution degrades capability the training data didn't reinforce (e.g. general instruction-following regresses after narrow-domain FT). LoRA forgets measurably less than full FT at matched task performance because frozen base weights preserve most general capability -- but LoRA also 'learns less,' so low rank can underfit tasks needing real new capability.

flashcards.q: How do serving stacks like vLLM run thousands of LoRA adapters on one GPU?
flashcards.a: One base model stays resident; each adapter is applied per-request via small batched matmuls rather than merged into a separate full model copy. Because the adapter matmuls are tiny relative to the base forward pass, throughput stays close to serving the base model alone.

flashcards.q: State the RAG-vs-fine-tuning decision rule in one sentence.
flashcards.a: If the failure looks like 'the model doesn't know a fact,' use retrieval; if it looks like 'the model knows it but does the wrong thing with it' (format, tone, behavior), try a better prompt first, then fine-tune.

flashcards.q: Why does fine-tuning to inject knowledge fail in production, specifically?
flashcards.a: Facts baked into weights are frozen at training time -- the model recites them correctly right after training, then gives stale or fabricated answers as the underlying facts change, and every update requires a full retrain. Retrieval updates immediately when the index changes and provides provenance fine-tuning can't.

flashcards.q: What data quality rule of thumb should guide whether to attempt fine-tuning?
flashcards.a: 1,000 hand-curated, diverse examples routinely beat 100,000 noisy ones. Below a few hundred genuinely high-quality examples, the model overfits to incidental patterns rather than the intended general behavior, often invisible until tested out-of-domain.

flashcards.q: Give a legitimate (non-knowledge-injection) reason to fine-tune.
flashcards.a: Distilling a long system prompt / few-shot pattern into weights to cut per-call token cost at volume -- this is teaching form/behavior, not facts, as long as the examples don't themselves embed facts that would get memorized.
